problems.title: Reversed vortex constant makes the prescribed dominant matching interval root-free
problems.location: PDF15 Theorem2.5 Cn; PDF21(3.19)-(3.21); PDF26(4.11); PDF28-30 Proposition4.6 and4.24-4.27; PDF33/35 Theorem4.7; PDF84-85 AppendixB
assumptions: Actual positive degree2 vortex, not freely chosen C2
Analytic C2<=2-2log15 proved by Pohozaev and exact ground-state identity
mu in exactly prescribed fixed positive interval
Positive q sufficiently small, rho=(q/|logq|)^(1/3),r0=exp(rho/q)/sqrt2,epsilon=mu exp(-pi/4q),k=epsilon/q
All overlap, smallness, intermediate Bessel and inner radius restrictions hold uniformly
problems.proof:
## P1: C_n sign, exact core matching counterexample
Actual source images: pp15,20,21,23,26-30,33,76,84-85. The definition is C_n=lim[A(r)-n^2 log r], A=int_0^r t f0^2(1-f0^2), not its negative.
Exact phase integral is v_in=q[-A+k^2 B]/(r f0^2), B=int_0^r t f0^2.
Thus v_in=-q[n^2(1+k^2)log r+C_n]/r+q k^2 r/2+q O(log r/r^3)+q k^2 O(1/r).
The source prints the opposite signs for C_n and k^2 r/2 in (3.21)/(4.11), and propagates +C_n into (4.26).

Independent energy proof, not a numerical assumption:
E_R(u)=int_0^R [r u'^2+n^2 u^2/r+(r/2)(1-u^2)^2].
For P=r^2 f'^2/2-n^2 f^2/2-r^2(1-f^2)^2/4, the ODE gives P'=-r(1-f^2)^2/2. The stated core and far-field asymptotics make P(0)=0 and P(infty)=-n^2/2. Hence J=int_0^infty r(1-f^2)^2=n^2.
The ODE also gives A(R)=int_0^R[r f'^2+n^2 f^2/r]-R f f'. Therefore C_n=E_ren(f)-n^2/2.
Writing g=f h and differentiating gives exactly
E_R(g)-E_R(f)=int r f^2 h'^2+(1/2)int r(g^2-f^2)^2+[r f f'(h^2-1)]_0^R.
Choose g=min((r/L)^n,1); it is continuous, piecewise C1 and locally H1, and the intermediate boundary terms cancel. Both endpoint terms vanish by the stated asymptotics. No unsupported global minimizer theorem is needed.
Direct integration gives E_ren(g)=n-n^2 log L+n^2 L^2/[2(n+1)(2n+1)].
With L^2=(n+1)(2n+1), C_n<=n-(n^2/2)log((n+1)(2n+1)); in particular C_2<=2-2log15<0.

Take the actual n=2 vortex, J_mu=[exp(-C_2/4-gamma),3exp(-C_2/4-gamma)], rho=(q/|log q|)^(1/3), r0=exp(rho/q)/sqrt2, epsilon=mu exp(-pi/(4q)), k=epsilon/q. The paper's cutoff exponent equals 1-log(r0)/log(1/epsilon) and tends to1 uniformly on J_mu. All overlap hypotheses hold for positive sufficiently small q: r0 large, kr0->0, 1/(q r0)->0, rho->0 and q|log q|/rho->0.
Using the convergent I_{+-inq} series and K connection formula, the exact outer logarithmic derivative at R=epsilon r0 has phase -pi/2+x, x=nq log r0+nq log(mu/2)-arg Gamma(1+inq)=O(rho). Its sine is bounded away from0. The differentiated series remainders are O(R^2), not merely a formal differentiation of an uncontrolled expansion.
Consequently
(r0/q)(v_in-v_out)=-C_n+n^2 log(mu/2)+gamma n^2+O(1/|log q|)+o(1),
uniformly on the fixed interval. The inner errors O(log r0/r0^2)+O(k^2 r0^2)+O(k^2 log r0) vanish. The outer tangent error is O(rho^3/q)=O(1/|log q|); the Bessel-series error after normalization is O(R^2/q^2).
For n2, the difference is >=-2C2-4log2+o(1)>=4(log(15/2)-1)+o(1)>0.
Thus the exact second equation (4.24) has no root in the prescribed interval, irrespective of a0,b0. This disproves Proposition4.6 with all its matching hypotheses.
Moreover the stated full-solution remainders normalize to o(1): inner O(q^2 log^3 r0)=O(1/|log q|), outer O(eta/(q^2 r0)+1/(q^3 r0^2)). They cannot close the fixed positive gap.
Repair requires +C_n/n^2 in the selected exponential factor with the present C_n definition, or a consistent change of definition throughout. A fully repaired global existence/uniqueness theorem is not proved here. The unconditional result is false dominant matching and failure of the core prefactor derivation, not a claim about every conceivable global branch.
problems.impact: Proposition4.6 exact phase equality has no root anywhere in permitted mu interval. Main prefactor selection and its proof fail; no independent universal no-spiral claim.
problems.correction: Use exact integral signs and +Cn/n² prefactor with present Cn definition; reselect interval and reconstruct phase matching.
problems.repair_verification: Corrected local asymptotic and positive-gap proof complete; global corrected existence/uniqueness not certified.

check.independent_reasoning: Root checked the exact phase integral and both constant/k2 signs, then reconstructed Pohozaev J=n2 and the ground-state energy identity. The admissible piecewise-power trial function optimized at L2=(n+1)(2n+1) gives C2<=2-2log15 without assuming a minimizing theorem or numerical value. In the paper's full prescribed mu interval, the exact matching gap is at least4(log(15/2)-1)+o(1)>0. All smallness/overlap relations coexist as q->0 and a0,b0 do not enter this equation. This refutes Proposition4.6 and its prefactor derivation, not every global spiral or a fully corrected existence theorem.

problems.title: Physical wavenumber retains dispersion-parameter dependence
problems.location: PDF6 Theorem1.5/Remark1.6; PDF12-13 Lemma2.3; PDF15-16 conversion
assumptions: Same positive small q<1/3
Physical pairs(0,q) and(1,(1+q)/(1-q)); both |alpha-beta|<1
Normalized selected k in(0,1), positive rescalings, nonzero frequencies
Exact scaled profiles preserve every core, winding, zero and far-field condition
problems.proof:
## P2: physical alpha dependence and oddness
Use physical alpha=A to distinguish it from the outer cutoff exponent.
For a normalized solution with k in (0,1), let D=1-A q(1-k^2), beta=(A+q)/(1-A q), a=sqrt D, delta^2=D/(1-A q), Omega=-(A+q(1-k^2))/D.
Then physical amplitude and phase are delta^-1 F(r/a), chi(r/a), and frequency Omega. Direct substitution into both real and imaginary CGL equations gives zero exactly; root symbolic check verifies these algebraic residuals. The physical wavenumber is K=k/sqrt D, and (1-k^2)/delta^2=1-K^2.
For 0<q<1/3, the pairs (A,beta)=(0,q),(1,(1+q)/(1-q)) have the same q, both |A-beta|<1, nonzero Omega, positive scaling and 0<K<1. The second K is strictly larger. The universal existence-plus-q-only uniqueness assertion in Theorem1.5 is therefore contradictory: its solution at the first pair maps exactly to a solution at the second.
The regular core, integer n, unique zero and far-field conditions are preserved by positive radial/amplitude scaling.
For fixed A nonzero, normalized odd kappa gives K(A,-q)=-kappa(q)/sqrt(1+Aq(1-kappa(q)^2)), not -K(A,q). Conjugation changes A as well as q.
Repair K=K(A,q). For bounded fixed A, the additional factor is 1+O(q), so this issue alone does not change the stated leading exponential accuracy. The separate C_n problem does.
No proof of normalized global existence is smuggled into the counterexample: it is a direct contradiction to the universal theorem's own asserted existence and selection, or an explicit transform of any actual normalized branch.
problems.impact: Exact q-only selection in the original equation contradicts exact transformation; fixed-alpha oddness also false. Leading fixed-bounded-alpha relative asymptotic accuracy survives this issue alone.
problems.correction: State K(alpha,q)=kappa(q)/sqrt(1-alpha q(1-kappa²)); retain amplitude/spatial/frequency scalings.
problems.repair_verification: Exact real/imaginary PDE residuals and far-field identity verified in primary Sympy exit0. No independent proof of normalized existence imported.

check.independent_reasoning: The exact positive rescaling gives K=k/sqrt(1-Aq(1-k2)). Parameter pairs (A,beta)=(0,q) and (1,(1+q)/(1-q)) obey the restrictions for small positive q and preserve the actual normalized profile/core/zero/far-field conditions while changing physical K. Thus the physical q-only selection and fixed-A oddness are false. For fixed bounded A the relative factor is1+O(q), so this alone does not change the claimed leading relative accuracy.

problems.title: Inner fixed-point system is not equivalent to the stated ODE
problems.location: PDF59(6.4b),(6.6),h0; PDF60(6.7),(6.8),positive Green kernel; PDF61Lemma6.1; PDF63-64(6.14)-(6.18)
assumptions: Actual matching positive smallq,k<1,allowed b0 and rho
Base vortex and phase integral are paper's actual functions
Theorem6.6 norm implies delta v=O(s)
Regular Green test s^n lies in finite-interval weightedspace
Exact phase test g=c f0,w=c(c+2)/(rf0²) integral t f0⁴ has w0=0; tests claimed phase rewrite, not coupled amplitude
problems.proof:
## P3: inner fixed-point system is not the stated ODE
Exact page images pp59-61,63-64 confirm all signs.
With L_n=d_s^2+s^-1 d_s-(1+n^2/s^2), the paper's positive kernel
Kpsi=K_n(s)int_0^s t I_n(t)psi(t)dt+I_n(s)int_s^s1 t K_n(t)psi(t)dt
satisfies L_n Kpsi=-psi, since s(K_n'I_n-I_n'K_n)=-1.
Take psi=s^n on a finite interval: all integrals converge and the forcing is nonzero. The sign is not a convention once (6.7) is fixed as L_n delta g=+N1.
This also affects the actual nonlinear construction. Take allowed b0, positive smallq, k<1, and the actual matching rho. If both its fixed-point formula and (6.7) held, N1 would vanish and delta g would be0. Near0, ftilde=A s^n+O(s^(n+2)), vtilde=-d s+O(s^3), d>0, and htilde=H s^(n+2)+O(s^(n+4)), H nonzero under either of the inconsistent signs in its p59 definition. The stated norm gives delta v=O(s). Therefore H_nonlin[htilde,delta v]-H_nonlin[0,0]=O(s^(n+2)), whereas E[htilde]=8(n+1)H s^n+O(s^(n+2)). Thus N1[0,delta v]=-4(n+1)H s^n+O(s^(n+2)) is not0. The claimed fixed-point-to-ODE bridge cannot hold on this permitted branch.

Independently, exact subtraction from the original phase equation gives
w'+w/r+2(f0'/f0)w=g(g+2f0)-2(v0+w)(f0g'-f0'g)/(f0(f0+g)).
Equation6.6 has two coefficients1. Its later integral uses rf0^2, which corresponds to the coefficient2. Under s=sqrt2 r and the printed S2 normalization, the derivative term in R2 must have coefficient -2sqrt2, not+1 in6.16.
An exact phase-equation counterexample is g=c f0, c>0, and w=c(c+2)/(r f0^2)int_0^r t f0^4 dt. It has w0=0 and solves the original phase equation for f=(1+c)f0. In6.6 its residual is -(f0'/f0)w, nonzero. This witnesses the claimed phase rewrite only, not a solution of the coupled amplitude equation.
Correct the h0 sign, inverse sign, resolvent, phase coefficients and rescaling, then prove the corrected contraction and boundary parameterization. We do not certify all those repairs here. One Major problem groups the common inner-construction impact.
problems.impact: Actual b0 fixed point cannot also satisfy6.7; phase coefficients independently wrong. The inner family proof used by main matching is invalid as written.
problems.correction: Correct shift sign, negative inverse, resolvent, phase factors2 and scaled -2sqrt2 derivative coefficient; rebuild proof.
problems.repair_verification: Exact identities and origin contradiction verified. Correctly constructed inner-solution existence not disproved; repaired contraction not certified.

check.independent_reasoning: The positive inner Green kernel has L K=-Id, opposite to the required equation. The actual allowed b0 branch would force delta g=0 and N1=0, but the core expansion produces -4(n+1)H s^n nonzero. Root checked the Wronskian sign and phase-factor subtraction, including the scaled -2sqrt2 coefficient. The phase identity is tested as an identity, not misrepresented as a full coupled solution. The actual fixed-point-to-ODE construction fails.

problems.title: Outer theorem's cutoff-exponent uniformity is false
assumptions: epsilon exp(-pi/2q),k=epsilon/q,cutoffalpha log(1/2)/logepsilon in(0,1)
Rmin1/2,epsilon^(1-alpha)/q=2k->0 meets all uniform thresholds
Base K_iq nonzero positive,F0>=1/2,allfunctionsreal
Hypothetical claimed bounds and exact ODE right inverses; homogeneous boundary layer explicitly controlled
problems.proof:
## P4: outer cutoff exponent quantifier
Fix n1,mu1 in[1/2,3/2],eta1,a0 and epsilon=exp(-pi/(2q)), k=epsilon/q. Set cutoff alpha=log(1/2)/log epsilon so Rmin=1/2 and epsilon^(1-alpha)/q=2k->0. All stated hypotheses of4.3/5.3 hold for sufficiently small positiveq.
Their refined a0 estimate forces ||G||_2<=Cepsilon^2 and ||W||_2<=2Cqk^2, with C independentofalpha.
Let Vq=K_iq'/K_iq,Fq=sqrt(1-k^2 Vq^2-epsilon^2/R^2),V*=K0'/K0.
The integral representation in source(A.12) proves K_iq/K0=1+O(q^2) uniformly R>=1/2 by controlling the t^2 moment; its differentiated version and common far-field tails give weighted convergence of Vq' and Fq'/k^2->-V*V*'.
All base functions are real, Fq>=1/2, Fq+G>=1/3.
Exact N1 yields ||N1||_2<=Cqk^4. With P=Lambda1[epsilon^-2 N1], the real-order Green estimates give ||P||_2<=Cqk^4, ||P'||_2<=Ck^3, ||P''||_2<=Ck^2/q.
Every decaying G=A_q K0(sqrt2 R/epsilon)+P. AtR1/2 the assumed G bound controls A_qK0 byCepsilon^2. OnR>=1 the jth derivative of this homogeneous term has X2 norm<=Cepsilon^(2-j)exp(-c/epsilon), j0,1,2.
Therefore G'/k^2->0 and q^2 G''/k^2->0 on[1,infty). ExactN2/k^2->-2V*^2 V*' inX2.
The first-order Green formula gives
W(1)/k^2 -> -2/K0(1)^2 int_1^infty t K0(t)^2 V*(t)^2 V*'(t)dt <0.
Dominated convergence follows from |K_iq|<=K0, positive limiting denominator and exponential integrability. V*'=Var_R(cosh t)>0 follows by differentiating the positive integral forK0. This contradicts |W(1)|/k^2<=2Cq->0.
No formal far-field ansatz for W is used. The homogeneous layer was explicitly bounded, and no identification ofa withA_q was assumed.
Repair can restrict cutoffalpha>=a*>0, with uniform estimates actually rechecked. Actual matchingalpha->1 is outside this counterexample; this issue alone does not refute its final asymptotic.
problems.impact: Claimed refined a0 W estimate conflicts with strictly negative actual right-inverse limit. General outer theorem scope fails. Actual matching cutoffalpha->1 is outside counterexample.
problems.correction: Restrict cutoffalpha to [alpha_*,1) with genuinely uniform proof, or retain appropriate dependencies/extra k² terms.
problems.repair_verification: Rigorous derivative and dominated convergence contradiction supplied. Full amended estimates not certified; no main asymptotic refutation from this issue alone.

check.independent_reasoning: The theorem's cutoff quantifiers are uniform in alpha. Choosing Rmin=1/2 and alpha=log(1/2)/log(epsilon) meets the written restrictions yet the refined bound forces W(1)/k2->0. Exact Green kernels, controlled boundary layer and weighted convergence give a strictly negative integral limit. Positivity of Vstar'=Var(cosh t) proves strictness. The actual matching alpha->1 avoids this counterexample, a boundary expressly retained.

problems.title: Dominant outer lower domain includes negative phase derivative and nonreal amplitudes
problems.location: PDF24Proposition4.2iii/iv; PDF20Riccati and square root; PDF75-78AppendixA; PDF79LemmaA.3
assumptions: For derivative:n1,mu1,k=exp(-pi/2q)/q,r2,positive smallq
Rexactlowerendpoint,Kpositive,F0²->3/4>0

problems.proof:
## P5: dominant outer lower endpoint
For n1,mu1,epsilon=exp(-pi/(2q)),k=epsilon/q andr2, R=2epsilon is permitted byProp4.2iii.
Convergent small-argument Bessel series give K_iq(R)=q^-1(1+o1)>0 and R Vq(R)=-gamma q^2+o(q^2).
The exact Riccati identity gives R^2 Vq'(R)/q^2 ->gamma-1<0, and hence (partial_r v_out)(2)/q->(gamma-1)/4<0.
F0(R)^2->3/4>0, so all functions are real. Bounds1-log2<=gamma<=3/2-log2<1 prove the sign without decimals.
The cotangent comparison p78 has the wrong direction.
The stronger2e^2 threshold usedbyGreen estimates and the actualmatchingpoint avoid this case; thus this is a local range correction, Minor.
The additional literal(iv)/LemmaA3 lower-domain claim is also too broad for amplitude reality: n1,mu100 in[99,101],cutoffalpha1/2,Rmin=2e^2 exp(-pi/(2q)) meetits inequalities forsmallq, while F0²<=1-[100/(2e²)]²<0. The actual4.3 domain imposes a largephysicalr and avoids it.
problems.impact: Printed lower-domain conclusions false. Stronger Green domain and actual matching avoid these examples; no further main-proof harm established.
problems.correction: Use a justified larger monotonicity threshold and an explicit physical-radius or reality restriction.
problems.repair_verification: Negative derivative from exact Riccati, gamma<1 and convergent series; amplitude upper bound strictlynegative. Complete corrected monotonicity proof not supplied.

check.independent_reasoning: At n=mu1,r2 the Bessel denominator is positive, F0 squared tends3/4, and the exact Riccati equation yields derivative/q->(gamma-1)/4<0. The separate large-mu witness concerns amplitude reality. Neither reaches the actual much larger matching radius; the stronger Green domain and corrected comparison argument are counterevidence against a core monotonicity failure.

problems.title: Scope clarification for the real-valued zero-twist restriction
assumptions: The exact source p5 explicitly states that the rotated unknown is real-valued.
For alpha nonzero, a solution that remains in that real class has zero stationary residual.
The earlier complex ODE solution with U0=1/2 leaves this class and therefore does not satisfy all printed restrictions.
problems.proof: Direct substitution gives U_t=(1+i alpha)(Delta U+U-|U|^2U). If U is real-valued and alpha is nonzero, its imaginary part forces Delta U+U-U^3=0 and U_t=0, so the restricted solution also solves the printed real GL equation. If alpha=0 the equations already coincide. The earlier alpha1,U0=1/2 ODE has derivative3(1+i)/8 and immediately ceases to be real. It cannot establish the previous confirmed counterexample. The general complex dynamical conjugacy does fail, but the source's real-valued restriction prevents treating that general observation as an established error under all printed hypotheses.
